# Introduction

This vignette demonstrates the full Mossy Forest (MF) workflow on the **World Development Indicators (WDI)** dataset from the World Bank. We want to predict a country's **life expectancy at birth** from its development profile.

Many indicators are strongly correlated (a country rich on one economic axis tends to be rich on many), so a model can "explain" the outcome with almost any one of the redundant block as a stand in for the others. 

The vignette is separated in four stages:

1. Data loading and summary
2. WGCNA
3. Single MF run and output for exploration purposes
4. Nested cross validation comparing all six MF variants 

---

# Data

We first load the data (included in the package).

```{r packages}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# if (!require("devtools", quietly = TRUE))
#     install.packages("devtools")
# library(devtools)
# devtools::install_github("timothyzshen/mossyforest")

library(mossyforest)
library(WGCNA)
```

```{r data}
data(wdi)

wdi_X      <- as.data.frame(wdi$X)
wdi_y      <- wdi$y
wdi_labels <- wdi$labels   # indicator 

cat("Countries :", nrow(wdi_X), "\n")
cat("Indicators:", ncol(wdi_X), "\n")
cat("Outcome   : life expectancy at birth,",
    paste(round(range(wdi_y), 1), collapse = " - "), "years\n")
```

```{r results-cache, echo=FALSE}
mf_cache <- if (file.exists("wdi_results.rds")) readRDS("wdi_results.rds") else NULL
```

We have a $181 \times 501$ matrix where the outcome is a continuous quantity (years of life expectancy). This is a regression problem, so throughout we score models by **out of sample $R^2$** (and RMSE in years) rather than the AUC used in the classification vignettes.

## Feature correlation structure

Before fitting anything it is worth seeing why this is a hard selection problem. Most of these indicators move together. We summarise this by the distribution of absolute pairwise **Spearman** (rank) correlations among all indicators. We use Spearman rather than Pearson because development indicators are heavily skewed (GDP, population, and land area span orders of magnitude) and often related monotonically but non linearly. 

```{r cor-hist}
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of absolute pairwise Spearman correlations among the 501 indicators. The right tail marks blocks of mutually redundant features — exactly the structure MF is designed to navigate."
library(ggplot2)

cor_mat <- cor(wdi_X, method = "spearman")
off_diag <- abs(cor_mat[upper.tri(cor_mat)])

ggplot(data.frame(r = off_diag), aes(x = r)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#1F77B4", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.7, linetype = "dashed", color = "tomato") +
  labs(title    = "Pairwise redundancy among indicators",
       subtitle = sprintf("%.1f%% of pairs have |rho| > 0.7",
                          100 * mean(off_diag > 0.7)),
       x = "Absolute Spearman correlation", y = "Number of indicator pairs") +
  theme_bw()
```

---

# WGCNA Module Detection

Before running MF we perform WGCNA ourselves to build the network structure. `mf()` can run WGCNA internally, but doing it manually lets us select the parameters and inspect the modules before moving towards MF.

```{r wgcna-load}
options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
enableWGCNAThreads()
```

## Rank transform for the network

WGCNA builds its network from pairwise correlations, so it inherits Pearson's weakness on skewed data. On the raw indicators this leads to a network in which ~80% of indicators unassigned, not because they lack structure but because their monotonic associations do not show up as high linear correlations. We therefore rank transform every indicator before building the network which recovers a better network structure. This transform is used **only** to define modules, MF itself is fit on the raw
indicators (random forests are invariant to monotonic transforms, so this
changes the module labels, not the model).

```{r wgcna-rank}
wdi_Xnet <- as.data.frame(lapply(wdi_X, rank))
rownames(wdi_Xnet) <- rownames(wdi_X)
```

## Soft threshold power selection

WGCNA constructs a weighted co expression style network by raising pairwise correlations to a soft thresholding power $\beta$. The chosen power should make the resulting network approximately **scale free** ($R^2 \geq 0.8$) while keeping **mean connectivity** reasonably high. We use a **signed** network so that positively- and negatively associated indicators land in different modules.

```{r soft-threshold, eval=FALSE}
powers <- c(1:10, seq(12, 20, by = 2))

sft <- pickSoftThreshold(
  wdi_Xnet,
  powerVector = powers,
  networkType = "signed",
  verbose     = 0
)
```

```{r soft-threshold-plot, eval=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Left: scale free topology fit (R²) vs soft power. Right: mean network connectivity vs soft power. Choose the lowest power where R² ≥ 0.8 (dashed line)."

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1))

plot(sft$fitIndices[, 1],
     -sign(sft$fitIndices[, 3]) * sft$fitIndices[, 2],
     xlab = "Soft threshold power (β)",
     ylab = expression(paste("Scale free topology fit R"^2)),
     main = "Scale free fit",
     type = "n", ylim = c(0, 1))
abline(h = 0.8, lty = 2, col = "tomato", lwd = 1.5)
text(sft$fitIndices[, 1],
     -sign(sft$fitIndices[, 3]) * sft$fitIndices[, 2],
     labels = powers, col = "#1F77B4", cex = 0.9, font = 2)

plot(sft$fitIndices[, 1],
     sft$fitIndices[, 5],
     xlab = "Soft threshold power (β)",
     ylab = "Mean connectivity",
     main = "Mean connectivity",
     type = "n")
text(sft$fitIndices[, 1],
     sft$fitIndices[, 5],
     labels = powers, col = "#D62728", cex = 0.9, font = 2)
```

Signed networks need roughly double the power of unsigned ones to reach scale free topology. We choose **β = 10**, the lowest power where $R^2$ reaches 0.8 while mean connectivity is still distinguishable from zero.

## Module detection and dendrogram

```{r wgcna-modules, eval=FALSE}
SOFT_POWER <- 6L

net <- blockwiseModules(
  wdi_Xnet,
  power             = SOFT_POWER,
  networkType       = "signed",
  TOMType           = "signed",
  minModuleSize     = 10L,
  mergeCutHeight    = 0.25,
  deepSplit         = 2,
  numericLabels     = FALSE,
  pamRespectsDendro = FALSE,
  saveTOMs          = FALSE,
  verbose           = 0
)

table(net$colors)   # grey = unassigned (treated as the unassigned pool by MF)
```

```{r wgcna-dendro, eval=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Indicator dendrogram with module color bar. Grey = unassigned features — these form the unassigned pool in MF's split shadow mode."

plotDendroAndColors(
  net$dendrograms[[1]],
  net$colors[net$blockGenes[[1]]],
  "Module",
  dendroLabels = FALSE,
  hang         = 0.03,
  addGuide     = TRUE,
  guideHang    = 0.05,
  main         = "Indicator dendrogram and module colors"
)
p_dendro <- recordPlot()
```

```{r show-dendro, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Indicator dendrogram with module color bar. Grey = unassigned features — these form the unassigned pool in MF's split shadow mode."
if (!is.null(mf_cache) && !is.null(mf_cache$p_dendro))
  print(mf_cache$p_dendro)
```

### Module membership summary

```{r module-summary, eval=FALSE}
mod_tbl <- as.data.frame(table(Module = net$colors))
mod_tbl$Unassigned <- mod_tbl$Module == "grey"
mod_tbl <- mod_tbl[order(mod_tbl$Freq, decreasing = TRUE), ]
knitr::kable(mod_tbl, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "WGCNA module sizes (grey = unassigned pool).")
```

```{r show-module-summary, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(mf_cache) && !is.null(mf_cache$mod_tbl))
  knitr::kable(mf_cache$mod_tbl, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = "WGCNA module sizes (grey = unassigned pool).")
```

Grey indicators are **unassigned by WGCNA** and treated as the unassigned pool. On the rank transformed network this pool is modest with the remaining ~85% falling into a handful of coherent modules (a macro economic block, a health/sanitation block, a demographic block, and so on). 

### Eigengene based connectivity (kME)

Module eigengenes summarise each module's profile as a single representative vector. Correlating every indicator with each module eigengene gives its **module membership** ($k_{ME}$).

```{r kme, eval=FALSE}
MEs <- net$MEs
kME <- as.data.frame(signedKME(wdi_Xnet, MEs, outputColumnName = "kME"))

gene_kME <- vapply(seq_along(net$colors), function(i) {
  col <- paste0("kME", net$colors[i])
  if (col %in% colnames(kME)) kME[i, col] else NA_real_
}, numeric(1))
```

### Hub indicators

Intramodular **hub indicators** are the features most strongly correlated with their module's eigengene ($k_{ME}$ near 1).

```{r hub-genes, eval=FALSE}
hub_df <- data.frame(
  indicator = colnames(wdi_X),
  label     = wdi_labels[colnames(wdi_X)],
  module    = net$colors,
  kME       = gene_kME,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
hub_df <- hub_df[hub_df$module != "grey" & !is.na(hub_df$kME), ]

top_hubs <- hub_df[order(-hub_df$kME), ][seq_len(min(20L, nrow(hub_df))), ]
top_hubs_disp <- top_hubs[, c("label", "module", "kME")]
knitr::kable(top_hubs_disp, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Top 20 intramodular hub indicators by kME.")
```

```{r show-hubs, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(mf_cache) && !is.null(mf_cache$top_hubs_disp))
  knitr::kable(mf_cache$top_hubs_disp, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = "Top 20 intramodular hub indicators by kME.")
```

```{r hub-lollipop, eval=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Top 20 intramodular hub indicators ranked by eigengene based connectivity (kME), colored by WGCNA module."
library(ggplot2)

p_hub <- ggplot(top_hubs, aes(x = reorder(label, kME), y = kME, color = module)) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = label, y = 0, yend = kME), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_identity(guide = "legend", name = "Module",
                        breaks = unique(top_hubs$module),
                        labels = unique(top_hubs$module)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title    = "Top intramodular hub indicators",
       subtitle = "Ranked by eigengene based connectivity (kME)",
       x = NULL, y = expression(k[ME])) +
  theme_bw()
p_hub
```

```{r show-hub-lollipop, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Top 20 intramodular hub indicators ranked by eigengene based connectivity (kME), colored by WGCNA module."
if (!is.null(mf_cache) && !is.null(mf_cache$p_hub)) print(mf_cache$p_hub)
```

### Final module membership (kME refined)

Hierarchical clustering can leave borderline indicators misassigned at the dendrogram cut. As a final step, we reassign every indicator to the module whose eigengene it correlates with most strongly (its **maximum kME module**). 

```{r module-membership, eval=FALSE}
module_names <- sub("^kME", "", colnames(kME))
best_module  <- module_names[max.col(as.matrix(kME), ties.method = "first")]

module_membership <- best_module
names(module_membership) <- colnames(wdi_X)

# Recode grey (no strong eigengene correlation) → "unassigned" so MF
# recognises the unassigned pool
module_membership[module_membership == "grey"] <- "unassigned"

membership_xtab <- as.data.frame.matrix(
  table(clustering = net$colors, kME_refined = module_membership))
knitr::kable(membership_xtab,
             caption = "Dendrogram clustering vs kME refined membership (row = clustering color).")
```

```{r show-membership, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(mf_cache) && !is.null(mf_cache$membership_xtab))
  knitr::kable(mf_cache$membership_xtab,
               caption = "Dendrogram clustering vs kME refined membership (row = clustering color).")
```

# Single MF Run

We fit MF once on the full dataset using the module membership derived above and the **Python backend**, which provides exact TreeSHAP values and is much faster than the pure R fallback. This requires a
Python environment with `scikit-learn`, `shap`, and `numpy` (see `?mf_setup`).

```{r mf-setup, eval=FALSE}
mf_setup()
```

```{r single-run, eval=FALSE}
fit <- mf(
  X = wdi_X,
  y = wdi_y,
  module_membership = module_membership,
  select_params = select_control(unassigned_modules = "unassigned"),
  backend = "python",
  verbose = 1L,
  seed = 2026
)
```

## Stable set

```{r stable-set, eval=FALSE}
cat("Stable indicators selected:", length(fit$feature_list$feature_name), "\n")
head(sort(fit$stability_freq, decreasing = TRUE), 20)
```


## Stability plot

```{r plot-stability, eval=FALSE, fig.height=15}
#| fig-cap: "Shadow win frequency per feature. Filled points exceed the stability threshold and enter the stable set."
plot_stability(fit)
```

```{r show-stability, eval=TRUE, fig.height=15}
#| fig-cap: "Shadow win frequency per feature. Filled points exceed the stability threshold and enter the stable set."
if (!is.null(mf_cache)) print(mf_cache$p_stability)
```

The dashed horizontal line is the tuned `pi_thr`. The right panel shows the
unassigned pool with its own elbow detected threshold.

## Feature importance

```{r plot-importance, eval=FALSE, fig.height=12}

```

# Model Comparison: Three Way Split + Cross Validated Tuning

## Design

We compare **six MF variants** formed by two shadow modes × three cfRes options:

| Variant | Shadow mode | cfRes |
|---------|-------------|-----|
| `split` | split | none |
| `split_cfres` | split | standard |
| `split_mcfres` | split | marginal |
| `within` | within_module | none |
| `within_cfres` | within_module | standard |
| `within_mcfres` | within_module | marginal |

We proceed with the following:

0. **Modules from all data.** The WGCNA network / `module_membership` from the
   section above (built on all samples) is reused throughout.
   
1. **Vault a test set** (~20%, stratified) — held out once, scored once, at
   the very end.
   
2. **On the remaining ~80% (train):** 5 fold CV tunes the hyperparameter grid *and* compares the six variants on both performance (mean validation fold $R^2$) **and** stability (Nogueira $\hat\Phi$ of the stable set across folds).

3. **Select one variant** by a pre specified rule (below), refit every variant
   on the *full* train set, and report performance on the test set. 

Hyperparameters tuned jointly on the validation folds:

| Parameter | Grid | Default |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `screen_control(drop_fraction)` | 0.25 (fixed) | 0.25 |
| `select_control(pi_thr)` | 0.50, 0.60, 0.70 | 0.60 |
| `min_ntree` (screen + select) | 500 (fixed) | 500 |
| `n_reps` | 25 (fixed) | 50 |

All other parameters stay at package defaults.

**Selection rule** For each variant, hyperparameters are tuned by the predictive AUC. Variant *selection* then uses the **Nogueira size corrected stability index** $\hat\Phi$. Among variants whose $\hat\Phi$
falls within one SE of the maximum, we choose the most **parsimonious**. 

## Setup

```{r cv-load-pack}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(caret)
```

```{r cv-setup, eval=FALSE}
VARIANTS <- list(
  split       = list(shadow_mode = "split",         use_cfres = FALSE, cfres_scope = "unassigned"),
  split_cfres   = list(shadow_mode = "split",         use_cfres = TRUE,  cfres_scope = "unassigned"),
  split_mcfres  = list(shadow_mode = "split",         use_cfres = TRUE,  cfres_scope = "all_modules"),
  within      = list(shadow_mode = "within_module", use_cfres = FALSE, cfres_scope = "unassigned"),
  within_cfres  = list(shadow_mode = "within_module", use_cfres = TRUE,  cfres_scope = "unassigned"),
  within_mcfres = list(shadow_mode = "within_module", use_cfres = TRUE,  cfres_scope = "all_modules")
)

GRID <- expand.grid(
  screen_drop = 0.25,
  pi_thr      = c(0.50, 0.60, 0.70),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Vault ~20% as the held out test set; the rest is train.
set.seed(2026)
trainval_idx <- as.integer(caret::createDataPartition(
  wdi_y, p = 0.8, list = FALSE))
test_idx     <- setdiff(seq_along(wdi_y), trainval_idx)

X_tv   <- wdi_X[trainval_idx, ]; y_tv   <- wdi_y[trainval_idx]
X_test <- wdi_X[test_idx, ];     y_test <- wdi_y[test_idx]

# Validation role = 5 fold CV within train
val_folds <- caret::createFolds(y_tv, k = 5, returnTrain = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("Train: %d  |  Test vault: %d\n", length(y_tv), length(y_test)))
```

## Fit and evaluate helper

```{r cv-helper, eval=FALSE}
fit_eval <- function(X_tr, y_tr, X_te, y_te, variant, grid_row) {

  sc  <- screen_control(
    drop_fraction = grid_row$screen_drop,
    min_ntree     = 500L
  )
  sl  <- select_control(
    pi_thr           = grid_row$pi_thr,
    n_reps          = 25L,
    min_ntree        = 100L,
    unassigned_modules = "unassigned",
    shadow_mode      = variant$shadow_mode,
    use_cfres = variant$use_cfres,
    cfres_scope        = variant$cfres_scope
  )

  fit <- tryCatch(
    mf(X_tr, y_tr,
       module_membership = module_membership,
       screen_params     = sc,
       select_params     = sl,
       backend           = "python",
       seed              = 42L,
       verbose           = 0L),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  stable <- if (!is.null(fit)) fit$feature_list$feature_name else character(0)
  if (length(stable) == 0L)
    return(list(r2 = NA_real_, rmse = NA_real_,
                n_stable = 0L, stable = character(0)))

  rf   <- ranger::ranger(
    y ~ ., num.trees = 300L, seed = 1L,
    data = data.frame(y = y_tr, X_tr[, stable, drop = FALSE])
  )
  pred <- predict(rf, data.frame(X_te[, stable, drop = FALSE]))$predictions

  sse <- sum((pred - y_te)^2)
  sst <- sum((y_te - mean(y_te))^2)

  list(
    r2       = 1 - sse / sst,
    rmse     = sqrt(mean((pred - y_te)^2)),
    n_stable = length(stable),
    stable   = stable
  )
}
```

## Cross validated tuning and stability

For each variant we sweep all 3 grid rows across the five validation folds, record each row's mean validation $R^2$, and lock the best scoring row. At that locked setting we keep the per fold stable sets, whose Nogueira $\hat{\Phi}$ is the variant's **stability**. 

```{r cv-tune, eval=FALSE}
jac_fn <- function(a, b)
  length(intersect(a, b)) / max(length(union(a, b)), 1L)

tune_one <- function(vname) {
  variant <- VARIANTS[[vname]]

  grid_res <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(GRID)), function(g) {
    per_fold <- lapply(seq_along(val_folds), function(fi) {
      vi   <- val_folds[[fi]]
      i_te <- vi; i_tr <- setdiff(seq_along(y_tv), vi)
      r <- fit_eval(X_tv[i_tr, ], y_tv[i_tr],
                    X_tv[i_te, ], y_tv[i_te],
                    variant, GRID[g, ])
      message(sprintf("[%s] g%02d fold%d — r2=%.3f n=%d",
                      vname, g, fi, r$r2, r$n_stable))
      r
    })
    list(
      r2   = mean(vapply(per_fold, `[[`, numeric(1), "r2"), na.rm = TRUE),
      r2s  = vapply(per_fold, `[[`, numeric(1), "r2"),
      sets = lapply(per_fold, `[[`, "stable")
    )
  })

  best_g <- which.max(vapply(grid_res, `[[`, numeric(1), "r2"))
  best   <- grid_res[[best_g]]

  jac <- mean(combn(length(best$sets), 2,
                    function(i) jac_fn(best$sets[[i[1]]], best$sets[[i[2]]]),
                    simplify = TRUE))

  message(sprintf(">>> [%s] DONE — best g%02d cv_r2=%.3f jaccard=%.3f",
                  vname, best_g, best$r2, jac))

  list(
    variant  = vname,
    best_row = GRID[best_g, ],
    cv_r2    = best$r2,
    cv_r2s   = best$r2s,
    jaccard  = jac,
    sets     = best$sets
  )
}

tune <- lapply(names(VARIANTS), tune_one)
names(tune) <- names(VARIANTS)
```

## Results

### Variant selection

For each variant, hyperparameters were tuned by predictive $R^2$. Variant selection itself uses the **Nogueira size corrected stability index** $\hat{\Phi}$ (Nogueira, Sechidis & Brown, 2018), which corrects the inflation that raw Jaccard exhibits when comparing variants with different stable set sizes. Among variants whose $\hat{\Phi}$ falls within one SE of the maximum, we select the most **parsimonious** (smallest $\bar{k}$).

```{r cv-select, eval=FALSE}
# helpers
.phi_hat <- function(sets, d) {
  M     <- length(sets)
  k_bar <- mean(sapply(sets, length))
  if (k_bar == 0 || k_bar >= d) return(NA_real_)
  pairs <- combn(M, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  sym_d <- sapply(pairs, function(idx) {
    a <- sets[[idx[1]]]; b <- sets[[idx[2]]]
    length(a) + length(b) - 2L * length(intersect(a, b))
  })
  v_obs  <- mean(sym_d) / d
  v_null <- 2 * k_bar * (d - k_bar) / d^2
  1 - v_obs / v_null
}

.phi_se <- function(sets, d) {
  M     <- length(sets)
  k_bar <- mean(sapply(sets, length))
  if (k_bar == 0 || k_bar >= d) return(NA_real_)
  v_null <- 2 * k_bar * (d - k_bar) / d^2
  pairs  <- combn(M, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  v_ij   <- sapply(pairs, function(idx) {
    a <- sets[[idx[1]]]; b <- sets[[idx[2]]]
    (length(a) + length(b) - 2L * length(intersect(a, b))) / d
  })
  sd(v_ij) / (sqrt(length(v_ij)) * v_null)
}

d_total <- ncol(wdi_X)

summary_tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tune, function(t) {
  phi    <- .phi_hat(t$sets, d_total)
  phi_se <- .phi_se(t$sets, d_total)
  k_bar  <- mean(sapply(t$sets, length))
  data.frame(
    Variant        = t$variant,
    CV_R2          = round(t$cv_r2, 3),
    CV_R2_SE       = round(sd(t$cv_r2s, na.rm = TRUE) /
                             sqrt(sum(!is.na(t$cv_r2s))), 3),
    Jaccard        = round(t$jaccard, 3),
    Phi            = round(phi, 3),
    Phi_SE         = round(phi_se, 3),
    k_bar          = round(k_bar, 1),
    `Best pi_thr`  = t$best_row$pi_thr,
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  )
}))

# 1 SE rule 
top     <- which.max(summary_tbl$Phi)
cutoff  <- summary_tbl$Phi[top] - summary_tbl$Phi_SE[top]
in_band <- summary_tbl[summary_tbl$Phi >= cutoff, ]
best_v  <- in_band$Variant[which.min(in_band$k_bar)]

knitr::kable(summary_tbl, align = "lccccccc",
             caption = "Validation fold performance and Nogueira stability (Φ̂) per variant.")
cat("Selected variant (1 SE on Φ̂, parsimony tiebreak):", best_v, "\n")
```

```{r show-summary, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(mf_cache))
  knitr::kable(mf_cache$summary_tbl, align = "lccccccc",
               caption = "Validation fold performance and Nogueira stability (Φ̂) per variant.")
```

### Pairwise variant comparison

The five validation folds give five paired $R^2$ values per variant. For all 15 pairs we report the mean difference in validation fold $R^2$. With only five folds, a significance test would have little power, so we do not report p values.

```{r pairwise, eval=FALSE}
pairs <- combn(names(VARIANTS), 2, simplify = FALSE)

pw <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(p) {
  a <- tune[[p[1]]]$cv_r2s
  b <- tune[[p[2]]]$cv_r2s
  data.frame(`Method A` = p[1], `Method B` = p[2],
             `ΔR2`      = round(mean(a - b, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(pw, caption = "Mean difference in validation fold R² between variants.")
```

```{r show-pairwise, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(mf_cache))
  knitr::kable(mf_cache$pw, caption = "Mean difference in validation fold R² between variants.")
```

### Nogueira stability

```{r phi-plot, eval=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Nogueira size corrected stability index (Φ̂) per variant with ±1 SE error bars. Unlike raw Jaccard, Φ̂ accounts for the expected overlap at each variant's selection size, enabling unbiased cross variant comparison."
library(ggplot2)

phi_df <- data.frame(
  Variant = summary_tbl$Variant,
  Phi     = summary_tbl$Phi,
  Phi_SE  = summary_tbl$Phi_SE
)

ggplot(phi_df, aes(x = reorder(Variant, Phi), y = Phi)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1F77B4", width = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Phi - Phi_SE, ymax = Phi + Phi_SE),
                width = 0.25, color = "grey30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title    = "Nogueira size corrected stability per variant",
       subtitle = "Error bars = ±1 SE  |  Dashed line = random selection null (Φ̂ = 0)",
       x = NULL, y = expression(hat(Phi))) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r show-jaccard, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Nogueira size corrected stability index (Φ̂) per variant with ±1 SE error bars."
if (!is.null(mf_cache)) print(mf_cache$p_jaccard)
```

### Final models and held out test evaluation

We refit **every** variant on the full train set at its locked hyperparameters, then score each on the test set. 

```{r final-models, eval=FALSE}
final_models <- lapply(names(VARIANTS), function(vname) {
  variant <- VARIANTS[[vname]]
  row     <- tune[[vname]]$best_row

  sc <- screen_control(
    drop_fraction = row$screen_drop,
    min_ntree     = 500L
  )
  sl <- select_control(
    pi_thr           = row$pi_thr,
    n_reps          = 25L,
    min_ntree        = 500L,
    unassigned_modules = "unassigned",
    shadow_mode      = variant$shadow_mode,
    use_cfres = variant$use_cfres,
    cfres_scope        = variant$cfres_scope
  )

  set.seed(42)
  fit <- mf(X_tv, y_tv,
            module_membership = module_membership,
            screen_params     = sc,
            select_params     = sl,
            backend           = "python",
            seed              = 42L,
            verbose           = 0L)

  stable <- fit$feature_list$feature_name
  rf <- ranger::ranger(
    y ~ ., num.trees = 300L, seed = 1L,
    data = data.frame(y = y_tv, X_tv[, stable, drop = FALSE])
  )
  pred <- predict(rf, data.frame(X_test[, stable, drop = FALSE]))$predictions
  sse  <- sum((pred - y_test)^2); sst <- sum((y_test - mean(y_test))^2)

  list(
    fit       = fit,
    test_r2   = 1 - sse / sst,
    test_rmse = sqrt(mean((pred - y_test)^2)),
    n_stable  = length(stable)
  )
})
names(final_models) <- names(VARIANTS)

test_tbl <- data.frame(
  Variant   = names(final_models),
  Test_R2   = round(vapply(final_models, `[[`, numeric(1), "test_r2"),   3),
  Test_RMSE = round(vapply(final_models, `[[`, numeric(1), "test_rmse"), 3),
  n_stable  = vapply(final_models, `[[`, integer(1), "n_stable"),
  Selected  = ifelse(names(final_models) == best_v, "<<", ""),
  row.names = NULL
)
knitr::kable(test_tbl, align = "lcccc",
             caption = "Held out test vault performance (selection made on validation only).")
```

```{r show-test, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(mf_cache))
  knitr::kable(mf_cache$test_tbl, align = "lcccc",
               caption = "Held out test vault performance (selection made on validation only).")
```


### Predictive value of the stable set

We compare a random forest trained on **all 501 indicators** against one trained on **only the MF stable set**, both scored on the same held out test vault with identical RF parameter settings. 

```{r perf-compare, eval=FALSE}
stable_final <- final_models[[best_v]]$fit$feature_list$feature_name

fit_rf_r2 <- function(feats) {
  rf   <- ranger::ranger(y ~ ., num.trees = 300L, seed = 1L,
                         data = data.frame(y = y_tv, X_tv[, feats, drop = FALSE]))
  pred <- predict(rf, data.frame(X_test[, feats, drop = FALSE]))$predictions
  sse  <- sum((pred - y_test)^2); sst <- sum((y_test - mean(y_test))^2)
  c(r2 = 1 - sse / sst, rmse = sqrt(mean((pred - y_test)^2)))
}

m_full   <- fit_rf_r2(colnames(X_tv))
m_stable <- fit_rf_r2(stable_final)

perf_tbl <- data.frame(
  `Feature set` = c(sprintf("Full (%d indicators)", ncol(X_tv)),
                    sprintf("MF stable set (%d)", length(stable_final))),
  n_features    = c(ncol(X_tv), length(stable_final)),
  Test_R2       = round(c(m_full["r2"],   m_stable["r2"]),   3),
  Test_RMSE     = round(c(m_full["rmse"], m_stable["rmse"]), 3),
  check.names   = FALSE, row.names = NULL
)
knitr::kable(perf_tbl, align = "lccc",
             caption = "Held out test performance: full feature set vs MF stable set.")
```

```{r show-perf, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(mf_cache) && !is.null(mf_cache$perf_tbl))
  knitr::kable(mf_cache$perf_tbl, align = "lccc",
               caption = "Held out test performance: full feature set vs MF stable set.")
```

### Top stable indicators by SHAP

The most influential indicators, ranked by **mean |SHAP|** (average absolute contribution to the life expectancy prediction across countries), with their WGCNA module, effect **direction**, and cross fit selection stability. Direction is the sign of the Spearman correlation between each indicator's value and its SHAP value. **+** increases the predicted average, indicating higher life expectancy. **−** decreases it. Indicators whose SHAP–value relationship is non monotone are flagged *ambiguous*.

```{r shap-final, eval=FALSE}
best_fit <- final_models[[best_v]]$fit

sh <- best_fit$final_SHAP
sh$score <- if (!is.null(sh$mean_abs_shap)) sh$mean_abs_shap else abs(sh$variable_importance)
sh <- sh[order(-sh$score), ]

shap_tbl <- data.frame(
  Indicator     = unname(wdi_labels[sh$feature_name]),
  Module        = sh$module_membership,
  `Mean |SHAP|` = round(sh$score, 4),
  Direction     = if (!is.null(sh$direction))
                    ifelse(sh$direction_ambiguous, "ambiguous",
                    ifelse(sh$direction > 0, "+ (promotes)", "− (suppresses)"))
                  else NA_character_,
  Stability     = if (!is.null(sh$stability_freq)) round(sh$stability_freq, 3) else NA_real_,
  check.names   = FALSE,
  row.names     = NULL
)[seq_len(min(10L, nrow(sh))), ]

knitr::kable(shap_tbl, align = "lcccc",
             caption = "Top 10 stable indicators by mean |SHAP| (deployed model).")
```

```{r show-shap, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(mf_cache) && !is.null(mf_cache$shap_tbl))
  knitr::kable(mf_cache$shap_tbl, align = "lcccc",
               caption = "Top 10 stable indicators by mean |SHAP| (deployed model).")
```
